case_studies.title: Multi-LCB: Extending LiveCodeBench to Multiple Programming Languages
case_studies.abstract: LiveCodeBench (LCB) has recently become a widely adopted benchmark for evaluating large language models (LLMs) on code-generation tasks. By curating competitive programming problems, constantly adding fresh problems to the set, and filtering them by release dates, LCB provides contamination-aware evaluation and offers a holistic view of coding capability. However, LCB remains restricted to Python, leaving open the question of whether LLMs can generalize across the diverse programming languages required in real-world software engineering. We introduce Multi-LCB, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of limited language support in LiveCodeBench, a benchmark for evaluating large language models on code-generation tasks. The authors built Multi-LCB, which extends LiveCodeBench to support multiple programming languages. The result is a more comprehensive benchmark for evaluating language models in real-world software engineering scenarios.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on evaluating language models for code generation tasks, but IT consultants may consider this when advising on AI-powered coding tools.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Paper introduces a new benchmark, but its applicability is unclear at this stage. The potential to measure LLMs across multiple languages could be valuable for assessing real-world software engineering abilities. IT engineers may not be able to use this within 90 days, but it could have significant long-term value.

case_studies.title: AgentFinVQA: A Deployable Multi-Agent Pipeline for Auditable Financial Chart QA
case_studies.abstract: Financial chart question answering in regulated settings demands more than accuracy: practitioners must know which answers to trust before acting on them, and many institutions cannot send client data to external model providers. Yet existing chart-QA agents are accuracy-focused and opaque, and most assume proprietary API access; to our knowledge, none combines auditability with on-premise deployability without significant accuracy compromise. We present AgentFinVQA, a multi-agent pipeline that decomposes each query into planning, OCR, legend grounding, visual inspection, and verification, rec
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of trusted financial chart question answering in regulated settings by building a deployable multi-agent pipeline called AgentFinVQA, which provides auditable and accurate results. The pipeline can be deployed on-premise without sending client data to external providers. The result is a more trustworthy and transparent financial chart question answering system.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage financial data infrastructure, here is what to do: review your current chart question answering systems for auditability and on-premise deployability, consider AgentFinVQA as a potential solution, and evaluate its compatibility with your existing systems.
case_studies.score_reasoning: High novelty and IT relevance given on-premise deployability and auditability of financial chart question answering. However, value 90 days is 0 as it's unclear how this can be applied within 90 days.

case_studies.title: TelcoAgent: A Scalable 5G Multi-KPM Forecasting With 3GPP-Grounded Explainability
case_studies.abstract: Key Performance Measurement (KPM) forecasting is essential for proactive network management of 5G and next-generation telecom networks. However, existing machine learning (ML) approaches face significant limitations in scalability and explainability, restricting their effectiveness in real-world deployments. We propose TelcoAgent, a foundation model-based framework that enables accurate, scalable, and explainable forecasting of multiple KPMs across diverse network cells without the need for site-specific training. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of scalability and explainability in Key Performance Measurement forecasting for 5G networks by building a framework called TelcoAgent, resulting in accurate and explainable forecasting of network performance. The framework enables proactive network management without needing site-specific training. This is relevant to telecom network management, not general cloud infrastructure.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage telecom network infrastructure, here is what to do: review your current KPM forecasting approach, consider adopting TelcoAgent for more accurate and explainable forecasting, and assess its scalability for your network. This flags a risk: if your organisation uses existing ML approaches for KPM forecasting, check their limitations in scalability and explainability immediately. Not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Uncertainty Decomposition for Clarification Seeking in LLM Agents
case_studies.abstract: Recent position papers argue that the classical aleatoric/epistemic uncertainty framework is insufficient for interactive large language model (LLM) agents and call for underspecification-aware, decomposed, and communicable uncertainty representations that can unlock new agent capabilities such as proactive clarification seeking and shared mental-model building. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of uncertainty in large language model agents by decomposing and communicating uncertainty, which can improve agent capabilities. The authors built a method for prompt-based estimation to address practical deployment constraints. The result is a new approach to uncertainty representation that can enable proactive clarification seeking and shared mental-model building.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on improving large language model agents and does not relate to cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.score_reasoning: High novelty and some potential real-world impact, but low monetisation potential and value within 90 days. Novelty primarily in AI/ML, but deployment constraints suggest this may have some it relevance. However, no clear path to immediate value or real-world impact.

case_studies.title: Analyzing Defensive Misdirection Against Model-Guided Automated Attacks on Agentic AI Systems
case_studies.abstract: Agentic AI systems increasingly rely on language-model components to interpret instructions, process external data, invoke tools, and coordinate with other agents. These capabilities make prompt-injection and jailbreak attacks more consequential, especially as attackers adopt model-guided automation to scale probing, prompt refinement, and response evaluation. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of model-guided automated attacks on Agentic AI systems by analyzing defensive misdirection, the authors built a probabilistic model to study the attack-defense setting, and the result shows limitations of conventional detect-and-block defenses. The study focuses on the security of AI systems, which may not directly impact cloud infrastructure management. The research highlights the vulnerability of AI systems to automated attacks.
case_studies.it_breakdown: This flags a risk: if your org uses Agentic AI systems with language-model components, check your defense mechanisms immediately to ensure they are not relying solely on detect-and-block methods. Not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work, but relevant to teams managing AI-powered systems. Review your AI system's security protocols to mitigate potential prompt-injection and jailbreak attacks.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty (8) - reveals an IT angle on an emerging threat. IT Relevance (2) - deals with agentic AI, but no direct impact on commonly used tools. Value (3) - shows that conventional defense may not work, potentially useful for someone deploying AI systems.

case_studies.title: UltraQuant: 4-bit KV Caching for Context-Heavy Agents
case_studies.abstract: Context-heavy agents place unusual pressure on the key-value (KV) cache: long prefixes are reused across many short turns, while concurrency determines whether the serving system can keep GPUs utilized. We study 4-bit KV-cache compression for this setting, using TurboQuant-style rotation and codebook quantization as a quality anchor and vLLM FP8 KV caching as the deployment anchor. We report three contributions. First, we frame 4-bit KV caching around multi-round agent workloads where task quality, cache residency, and serving throughput must be measured jointly. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of inefficient key-value caching for context-heavy agents by building a 4-bit KV caching system, resulting in improved cache compression and utilization. The UltraQuant system uses rotation and codebook quantization to achieve this. This has potential implications for optimizing cloud infrastructure that supports AI and machine learning workloads.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure that supports AI and machine learning workloads, here is what to do: review your current key-value caching setup, consider implementing 4-bit KV caching compression, and assess the potential performance gains for your specific use case.
case_studies.score_reasoning: UltraQuant's focus is on AI performance, specifically for context-heavy agents. It shows surprising efficiency in certain cases, but lacks real-world IT relevance, and no obvious value for IT engineers within 90 days.
